abstract: The precise timing of neural progenitor differentiation and cell fate specification is critical for establishing the size and cellular diversity of the cerebral cortex. However, how chromatin regulators control the temporal progression of neurogenesis remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the cooperative roles of Euchromatic Histone Lysine Methyltransferases 1 and 2 (EHMT1 and EHMT2) in mouse cortical neurogenesis. We demonstrate that EHMT1- and EHMT2-mediated H3K9me2 deposition is dispensable for H3K9me3, and that these histone marks occupy distinct chromatin regions. Combined loss of EHMT1 and EHMT2 reduces neural progenitor proliferation, promotes differentiation, and disrupts the transition from deep- to upper-layer neurogenesis, resulting in microcephaly and altered neuronal subtype composition in the postnatal cortex. We further show that EHMT2 directly regulates genes involved in neurogenesis and upper-layer neuron specification through both transcriptional repression and activation. Moreover, EHMT1 and EHMT2 suppress the premature expression of synaptic genes in neural progenitors through complementary mechanisms involving H3K9me2-associated chromatin compaction and H3K9me2-independent silencing in cooperation with PRDM16. Together, these findings establish EHMT1 and EHMT2 as central regulators of the temporal control of cortical neurogenesis and reveal molecular mechanisms that may contribute to the pathogenesis of Kleefstra syndrome.
